messages:
seung: quick heads-up — noticed a p99 spike during the 11:10 PDT traffic burst after the kernel-selector packing change landed. p95 stayed fine, but p99 doubled for ~3 minutes.

laila: ugh. any idea whether this is KV coldness or kernel fallback?

seung: digging — initial traces show a lot of requests hitting a fallback slowpath (scalar kernel) when microbatch sizes were small and kv cache miss rate was higher. i pasted a tiny snippet from the profiler: 
```
flame: kernel_path_switch -> 62%
flame: kv_lookup + prefetch -> 18%
flame: microbatch_queueing -> 8%
```

matt_r: hmm that kernel_selector change was trying to prefer fused kernels for 128+ tokens. but most requests in that burst were short (<=64) and the selector seemed to mis-classify slots after scale-up. possible race between prober and instance initialization.

olga: also seeing increased cold-handshake time on the new instances — grpc warmup delayed the kv prefill job because prober runs at lower priority. that delays KV priming ~400ms occasionally. combined with kernel fallback that explains the tail.

seung: proposed quick mitigations: 1) temporarily revert the packing override, 2) bump prober priority so prefill runs before serving, 3) increase transient microbatch cap from 8->16 for 30s during bursts to absorb variance. thoughts?

laila: +1 to bumping prober priority. reverting packing is safer if we want fast rollback. increasing microbatch cap might harm average latency — but helps p99? we need numbers.

matt_r: can we instead add a fast-path check: if instance age < 90s treat kernel decision conservatively (prefer compatibility kernel) until kv hit-rate stabilizes? avoids fallback thrash.

seung: good idea. i'll run an A/B in staging: 1) prober-priority bump + kernel conservative-for-young-instances, 2) revert packing. collect p95/p99 and kv-hit traces.

perf-bot: experiment created: exp-2145-handshake-stabilize. comparing traces between control and two variants. perf-bot will report after 30m.

olga: one more note — autoscaler surge policy currently adds nodes with no kv pre-warm. we could add a lightweight async prefill (few prefixes) for popular prefixes to reduce initial misses. cheap and targeted.

seung: agreed. i'll prototype targeted prefill in the filler job rather than full pre-warm. will post numbers here. thanks all :thumbsup:

matt_r: ping when you have the staging results. if good we can roll to canary and watch tail latency with the new heatmap view.

seung: will do — staging run started at 2145678920, ending ~2145679320. collecting logs + flamegraphs.
